subject: Elevated support authorization & residency - action items
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finco.com>, procurement@finco.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated support authorization & residency - action items

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the items we committed to follow up on related to support access, PII handling, and data residency: 

1) Elevated support / break-glass: you want a documented process where support engineers can request transient elevated access for incident triage with an approval window (max 2 hours), mandatory justification, and full session logging.

2) RBAC and least-privilege: FinCo needs role-mapped access for Support vs SRE vs Customer Ops; support should not have broad export permissions by default.

3) PII redaction / retention: confirm what elements you consider PII in payloads (SSNs, bank account numbers, full names + dob) and whether samples are ok for debugging.

4) Logging and audit evidence: you asked for examples of session logs (who/when/what) and tokenized request/response retention windows. We'll provide a snapshot of the last 30 days of support sessions (redacted) and the runbook that governs break-glass.

Next steps (owners):
- Redwood (Naomi): provide runbook + sample session logs and S3 snapshot by Thu EOD (attached when ready).
- Redwood (Ben): note-of-implementation for RBAC roles and available JIT tooling (ETA Mon).
- FinCo (Alex): confirm PII scope and whether a 30-day request/retention policy is acceptable or whether you require shorter windows.

Attachments to follow: support-runbook.pdf (runbook draft), s3-logging-snapshot.txt (redacted sample).

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Strategic Account Lead
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finco.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated support authorization & residency - action items

Thanks Naomi — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII scope: confirmed — SSN, full payment instrument numbers, full DOB, and government IDs are PII. Names and emails are considered identifiable but might be allowed in redacted form for troubleshooting. We cannot have full payment numbers in logs at any time.

- Retention: 30 days is acceptable for session metadata (who, when, actions). For payloads containing any PII we require either (a) immediate redaction before storage, or (b) encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys + an escape clause that forces deletion within 7 days unless we approve retention for a specific incident.

- Break-glass: approval must come from our on-call Security lead or an authorized manager; automated approvals are not sufficient. We also need assurance that the elevated session will be recorded and that a transcript and audit trail are delivered to our secure S3 bucket at /finco/support-audit/.

Can you confirm if Redwood supports delivering redacted transcripts + exporting audit bundles to our S3 (we have an existing cross-account role)?

— Alex

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@finco.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated support authorization & residency - action items

Alex — thanks for the clear PII/retention constraints. Quick responses inline and confirmed actions: 

- Payloads with high-sensitivity PII (payment instrument numbers, SSN) — we will require client-side redaction or tokenization before they land in logs. For debugging, we can accept truncated/masked samples (last 4 digits only).

- Retention: we can support the default 30-day metadata retention for session logs and a separate 7-day retention (auto-delete) policy for any stored payloads that include customer-approved PII snapshots. We will also provide the deletion confirmation artifact.

- Customer-managed keys: Redwood supports KMS integration allowing you to manage keys for stored payloads. We will provide the integration steps.

- Export to your S3: yes — we can push redacted transcripts and the audit bundle to a customer-controlled S3 destination via a cross-account role. We'll include the sample ACL/role policy for your cloud team to review.

Attached: support-runbook.pdf (draft with JIT steps), s3-logging-snapshot.txt (redacted sample). Ben — can you add the RBAC role mapping doc and the JIT implementation ETA to the runbook?

Alex — can you confirm who the on-call Security lead contact is for approval flows (name + email)? That will let us wire the approval webhook.

Thanks, Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Strategic Account Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@finco.com>
Cc: procurement@finco.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated support authorization & residency - action items

Looping in a quick ops confirmation — Ben, this is the implementation checklist I want in the runbook before I sign off: 

- RBAC matrix: explicit roles (Support_ReadOnly, Support_Triage_JIT, SRE_Full), scope-limited to the tenant (no cross-tenant exports).
- JIT step flow: request -> manager approval -> token issuance (time-limited) -> session recording -> auto-revoke.
- Audit artifacts: session transcript (redacted), activity log (who/what/when), and proof-of-deletion for any PII snapshots.
- Delivery: S3 push to FinCo cross-account + retention metadata sent to FinCo via signed manifest.
- Test plan: run one simulated break-glass with FinCo security to validate the webhook and S3 push (target Fri next week).

Alex — if that works please confirm the on-call security approver and whether Friday next week works for the simulation. Procurement — we'll include the SOC-2 reference and appendix in the runbook for your review.

— Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
